The project raised the pressure rating of about 20 miles of the existing Algonquin main line from 750 to 900 psig between Burrillville, Rhode Island and Mendon, Massachusetts. It replaced about 2.3 miles of existing pipe in short sections, built one new 545 foot 10 inch tie-in and a meter station at the Tiverton power plant, and raised the horsepower of two turbines at the Chaplin compressor station in Connecticut. It added up to 46,000 dekatherms per day of service to Tiverton Power Associates. So the 16 miles is mostly existing main line that was uprated, not a new lateral. New pipe is well under 1 mile, far below the 25 km floor. No separate row is justified. The existing Algonquin main line row (P0149) is the home for this capacity work.
